about: Reference values for the chaos-graph tests. Computed on 2026-11-10 by research scripts (Python, numba, mpmath). Each value was checked by the script that produced it; the planned second, independent recomputation did not run, so the TypeScript implementation's tests are the independent check. Lyapunov exponents use natural logarithms. Some systems here are outside the first release.

oracles.description: At K=1 the winding number equals the inverse golden mean (sqrt(5)-1)/2 at exactly one Omega. Computed: superstable cycles through theta=0 with winding numbers F_(n-1)/F_n (Newton on the lift F^q(0)=p at 240-bit precision, q up to 46368) extrapolated by iterated Aitken; the Fibonacci parameter differences shrink by the universal ratio delta = -2.83361 (literature -2.83361).

Winding number W = mean of (Omega - K/(2 pi) sin(2 pi theta_n)) over N=1e6 steps (1000 transient) at K=1, Omega=0.6066610634702 equals (sqrt(5)-1)/2. Observed over 5 initial phases: max |dev| 1.6e-08 (bounded-deviation rotation, error O(1/N)).

The 0/1 mode-locking tongue is |Omega| <= K/(2 pi) (fixed point sin(2 pi theta*) = 2 pi Omega/K exists); edge at K=1. Computed: bisection on Omega for the winding number (N=20000) changing from 0 to positive.

Left edge of the 1/2 mode-locking tongue at K=1 (saddle-node of the 2-cycle: F^2(theta)=theta+1, (F^2)'(theta)=1 on the lift); the right edge is 1 minus this value by symmetry, so W=1/2 exactly for Omega in [0.463017223, 0.536982777]. Value: mpmath Newton; computed: bisection on Omega for the measured winding number (N=20000 after 40000 transient) reaching 1/2.
oracles.source: computed (lowest-order perturbation theory gives 1/2 - K^2/(8 pi) = 0.460211)

oracles.description: For K=0 the map is a rigid rotation and the winding number equals Omega; value for Omega=0.3. Computed: mean phase advance over 1e5 steps.

Lyapunov exponent at Omega=1/3, K=4: mean of ln|1 - K cos(2 pi theta_n)| over N=1e6 steps after 1000 transient (theta kept mod 1). Value = mean over 32 initial phases; observed sd 5.8e-04, max |dev| 1.4e-03.
theta_6 from theta_0=0.1 at Omega=1/3, K=4; each step theta <- (theta + Omega - K/(2 pi) sin(2 pi theta)) mod 1 with mod = x - floor(x). Reference from 50-digit arithmetic; amplification bound 493.
theta_20 from theta_0=0.1 at K=1, Omega=0.6066610634702 (quasi-periodic, no error growth). Reference from 50-digit arithmetic; amplification bound 59.

Largest Lyapunov exponent at a=-1.4, b=1.6, c=1, d=0.7 (per-step QR with the analytic Jacobian, N=1e6 after 1000 transient). Value: mean of 12 runs of 5e7 steps. Scatter at N=1e6 over 32 initial conditions spread over [-2,2]^2: sd 2.9e-04, max |dev| 6.4e-04.
Second Lyapunov exponent, same method. Scatter at N=1e6: sd 6.2e-04, max |dev| 1.4e-03.

Every iterate satisfies |x| <= 1+|c| and |y| <= 1+|d|, so the picture always fits in [-(1+|c|),1+|c|] x [-(1+|d|),1+|d|]. Value: 1+|c| at the default; computed: max |x| over 5e7 iterates (max |y| = 1.5352 vs bound 1.7), which must not exceed it.
oracles.source: exact bound (the attractor nearly reaches it)

oracles.description: x_10 from (x_0,y_0)=(0.1,0.1) at a=-1.4, b=1.6, c=1, d=0.7; simultaneous update (x,y) <- (sin(a*y)+c*cos(a*x), sin(b*x)+d*cos(b*y)). Reference from 50-digit arithmetic; amplification bound 80.
y_10 of the same orbit.

Largest Lyapunov exponent at a=1.4, b=-2.3, c=2.4, d=-2.1 (per-step QR with the analytic Jacobian, N=1e6 after 1000 transient). Value: mean of 12 runs of 5e7 steps. Scatter at N=1e6 over 32 initial conditions spread over [-2,2]^2: sd 4.6e-04, max |dev| 1.1e-03.
Second Lyapunov exponent, same method. Scatter at N=1e6: sd 9.0e-04, max |dev| 1.9e-03.
Every iterate satisfies |x| <= 2 and |y| <= 2 (difference of a sine and a cosine), for all parameters. Computed: max(|x|,|y|) over 5e7 iterates at the default, which must not exceed 2.
x_6 from (x_0,y_0)=(0.1,0.1) at a=1.4, b=-2.3, c=2.4, d=-2.1; simultaneous update (x,y) <- (sin(a*y)-cos(b*x), sin(c*x)-cos(d*y)). Reference from 50-digit arithmetic; amplification bound 140.
y_6 of the same orbit.
Nonzero fixed points are x = y = +-sqrt(a-b-1); value of the positive one at a=2.75, b=0.2 (the origin is the third fixed point; all three are unstable). Computed: scipy fsolve on the map equations.
det J = b at every point (J = [[0,1],[-b, a-3y^2]]). Computed: central finite differences (h=1e-6) of the map at 4 points; allowed deviation 1e-8.
Largest Lyapunov exponent at a=2.75, b=0.2 (per-step QR, N=1e6 after 1000 transient). Value: mean of 12 runs of 5e7 steps. Scatter at N=1e6 over 32 initial conditions: sd 3.9e-04, max |dev| 1.0e-03.
Second Lyapunov exponent, same method. Scatter at N=1e6: sd 3.9e-04, max |dev| 1.1e-03.
lam1 + lam2 = ln(det J) = ln(b) = ln 0.2 for any orbit. Computed from a 1e6-step QR run; allowed deviation 1e-9.
x_8 from (x_0,y_0)=(0.1,0.1) at a=2.75, b=0.2, simultaneous update (x,y) <- (y, -b*x + a*y - y^3). Reference from 50-digit arithmetic; amplification bound 643.
y_8 of the same orbit.

Exact-arithmetic form for beta=2: x = k/M with the safe prime M = 2^52 - 2933 = 4503599627367563 (2 is a primitive root, so every k in 1..M-1 has period M-1), k <- 2k mod M. Value: k_1000 from k_0 = round(0.1*M) = 450359962736756 (all values < 2^53, exact in doubles). Computed by 1000 doublings; value from modular exponentiation 2^1000*k_0 mod M.

Time average of x for beta=2 is 1/2 (variance 1/12, measured 0.08340) using the exact integer form k <- 2k mod M, x=k/M, N=1e6 steps; over 32 initial k: sd 4.7e-04, max |dev| 8.6e-04. (A naive double orbit is identically 0 after at most 54 steps.)

Lyapunov exponent is ln(beta) for every orbit (slope beta everywhere): ln 2 for the dyadic map. Computed: growth rate (1/40) ln(|delta_40|/|delta_0|) of the separation of two exact rational orbits started 2^-60 apart (x0 = 1/3 and 1/3 + 2^-60, no wrap-around mismatch for 40 steps).

x_8 from x_0=0.3 at beta=2 with plain doubles, x <- (beta*x) mod 1 (exact rational orbit: 0.3,0.6,0.2,0.4,0.8,0.6,0.2,0.4,0.8). Amplification bound 511; safe because 8 steps are far from the collapse at step ~53.
x_6 from x_0=0.3 at beta=2.5 (beta-transformation), plain doubles. Reference from exact rational arithmetic; amplification bound 406.
In exact arithmetic x0=1/7 is 3-periodic under beta=2: 1/7 -> 2/7 -> 4/7 -> 1/7 (binary expansion 0.001001...). Value: third iterate. Computed with Python Fractions.

At alpha=4.9 the fixed point loses stability by period doubling at this beta (fixed point x with 2*alpha*x*exp(-alpha x^2)=1, smaller root x=0.108048212, beta = x - exp(-alpha x^2)); period 1 just below, 2 just above. Value: mpmath root; computed: independent Newton solve of f(x)=x, f'(x)=-1 (gmpy2, analytic derivatives).

At alpha=4.9 the period-doubling 'bubble' closes: the fixed point regains stability by a reverse period doubling at this beta (larger root x=0.601788761 of 2*alpha*x*exp(-alpha x^2)=1); period 2 just below, 1 just above. Same method as pd-first-beta-alpha4.9.
Period of the attractor at alpha=4.9, beta=-0.58 (the Wikipedia cobweb example). Computed: 400000 transient steps from x0=0.1, then smallest p<=64 with |x_(n+p)-x_n| < 1e-9.
The unique fixed point at alpha=6.2, beta=-0.5 (root of exp(-alpha x^2)+beta-x; multiplier -2.0445, repelling). Value: mpmath root; computed: double-precision bisection on [0,1].

Lyapunov exponent at alpha=6.2, beta=-0.5: mean of ln|2*alpha*x_n*exp(-alpha x_n^2)| over N=1e6 steps after 1000 transient. Value = mean over 32 initial conditions in [-0.5,0.5]; observed sd 3.8e-04, max |dev| 8.1e-04.

Every iterate satisfies beta < x <= 1+beta (f(0)=1+beta is the maximum of the map); on the attractor at alpha=6.2, beta=-0.5 the range is [f(1+beta), 1+beta] = [exp(-alpha/4)-0.5, 0.5]. Value: lower edge. Computed: minimum of a 2e6-step orbit from x0=0.1 (measured max 0.500000000).
x_10 from x_0=0.1 at alpha=6.2, beta=-0.5, plain iteration x <- exp(-alpha*x*x)+beta. Reference from 50-digit arithmetic; amplification bound 121.
x of the saddle fixed point on the attractor: x = (-(1-b)+sqrt((1-b)^2+4a))/(2a), y = b*x = 0.189406343126851, at a=1.4, b=0.3. Computed: 2-D Newton (mpmath) on the map equations.
x of the second fixed point: x = (-(1-b)-sqrt((1-b)^2+4a))/(2a), y = b*x = -0.339406343126851 (outside the attractor, on the basin boundary).

det J = -b at every point (J = [[-2a x, 1],[b, 0]]): constant area contraction by |b| per step with orientation reversal. Computed: central finite differences (h=1e-6) of the map at 4 points; allowed deviation 1e-8.

Largest Lyapunov exponent at a=1.4, b=0.3 (per-step Gram-Schmidt/QR on the Jacobian, natural log, N=1e6 steps after 1000 transient). Value: mean of 12 runs of 1e8 steps. Scatter at N=1e6 over 32 initial conditions: sd 2.5e-04, max |dev| 5.4e-04.
Second Lyapunov exponent, same method as lyapunov-1. Scatter at N=1e6: sd 2.5e-04, max |dev| 5.4e-04.
lam1 + lam2 = ln|det J| = ln(b) = ln 0.3 for any orbit and any run length (QR method). Computed: lam1+lam2 from a 1e6-step run; allowed deviation 1e-9.
Kaplan-Yorke (Lyapunov) dimension 1 + lam1/|lam2| from the N=1e6 exponents. Scatter over 32 initial conditions: sd 1.2e-04.
x_10 from (x_0,y_0)=(0,0) at a=1.4, b=0.3, simultaneous update (x,y) <- (1-a*x*x+y, b*x); first steps (1,0), (-0.4,0.3). Reference from 50-digit arithmetic; amplification bound 542.
y_10 of the same orbit (equals b*x_9).
First period doubling at b=0.3: the fixed point gets eigenvalue -1 at a = 3(1-b)^2/4. Computed: Brent root of det(DT(x*)+I) with the cycle found by Newton (double precision).
Second period doubling (2-cycle -> 4-cycle) at b=0.3: a = (1-b)^2 + (1+b)^2/4. Computed as pd-a1 for the 2-cycle.

Third period doubling (4-cycle -> 8-cycle) at b=0.3; later ones: a4=1.051125662, a5=1.056563758, a6=1.057730840, ratios (a_(k-1)-a_(k-2))/(a_k-a_(k-1)) = 4.808, 4.486, 4.647, 4.660 (-> Feigenbaum delta), accumulation about 1.058049. Value: 40-digit mpmath Newton on T^4(x,y)=(x,y), det(DT^4+I)=0; computed: independent double-precision Brent root with scipy.

Accumulation point of the period-doubling cascade at b=0.3 (onset of chaos). Computed: a6 + (a6-a5)/(delta-1) from the 40-digit bifurcation values up to period 32->64 (Aitken on a3..a6 gives 1.0580498).
oracles.source: Derrida, Gervois, Pomeau, J. Phys. A 12 (1979) 269: a_inf = 1.058048...

oracles.description: det J = u^2 at every point (rotation by t(x,y) composed with scaling by u; the t-dependence cancels), u=0.9. Computed: central finite differences (h=1e-6) of the map at 4 points; allowed deviation 1e-8.

x of the saddle fixed point embedded in the attractor at u=0.9 (y = 0.246896772711013, eigenvalues -2.3897 and -0.3390). Value: 40-digit mpmath Newton on the map equations; computed: scipy fsolve in double precision.
y of the same fixed point.

Largest Lyapunov exponent at u=0.9 (per-step QR with the analytic Jacobian, N=1e6 after 1000 transient). Value: mean of 12 runs of 5e7 steps. Scatter at N=1e6 over 32 initial conditions: sd 4.4e-04, max |dev| 1.2e-03.
Second Lyapunov exponent, same method. Scatter at N=1e6: sd 4.4e-04, max |dev| 1.2e-03.
lam1 + lam2 = ln(det J) = 2 ln(u) = 2 ln 0.9 for any orbit. Computed from a 1e6-step QR run; allowed deviation 1e-9.

x_8 from (x_0,y_0)=(0.1,0.1) at u=0.9; each step t = 0.4 - 6/(1+x^2+y^2), (x,y) <- (1+u(x cos t - y sin t), u(x sin t + y cos t)) simultaneously. Reference from 50-digit arithmetic; amplification bound 80.
y_8 of the same orbit.

At u=0.9 the chaotic attractor coexists with an attracting spiral fixed point at (x,y) = (2.972131617911, 4.145946421396) (eigenvalue modulus 0.9); initial conditions far from the origin converge to it instead of the strange attractor. Value: 40-digit mpmath Newton; computed: 5000 plain iterations from (10,10).
First period doubling (fixed point x*=1-1/r has multiplier 2-r = -1): r1 = 3. Computed: Newton continuation of the fixed point to multiplier -1 at 240-bit precision.
Second period doubling (2-cycle multiplier 4+2r-r^2 = -1): r2 = 1+sqrt(6). Computed: Newton solve of f^2(x)=x, (f^2)'(x)=-1.

Third period doubling (4-cycle multiplier = -1; algebraic number, no simple closed form). Value: Newton solve (analytic derivatives, 240-bit) of f^4(x)=x, (f^4)'(x)=-1 at 240-bit precision; computed: independent mpmath solve with numerical differentiation.
oracles.source: literature 3.544090359 (e.g. Strogatz, Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos, sec. 10.2: 3.54409)

oracles.description: Fourth period doubling (8-cycle multiplier = -1). Value: Newton solve (analytic derivatives, 240-bit) of f^8(x)=x, (f^8)'(x)=-1 at 240-bit precision; computed: independent mpmath solve with numerical differentiation.

Accumulation point r_inf of the period-doubling cascade (onset of chaos). Computed: superstable parameters R_k (f^(2^k)(1/2)=1/2) for k<=18 at 240-bit precision, iterated Aitken extrapolation; the same limit from the bifurcation values r_k agrees to 1e-28.
Finite Feigenbaum estimate (r3-r2)/(r4-r3) from the bifurcation values above (the previous ratio (r2-r1)/(r3-r2) is 4.751446).
Feigenbaum constant delta = lim (R_(k-1)-R_(k-2))/(R_k-R_(k-1)). Computed: ratios of superstable parameters up to period 2^18, iterated Aitken extrapolation.

Feigenbaum constant alpha = lim -d_k/d_(k+1), d_k = f_(R_k)^(2^(k-1))(1/2) - 1/2 (signed distance from the critical point to the nearest point of the superstable 2^k-cycle). Computed up to k=18 with Aitken extrapolation.
Parameter where the 2-cycle is superstable (contains x=1/2): R1 = 1+sqrt(5). Computed: Newton solve of f^2(1/2)=1/2.
Tangent (saddle-node) bifurcation creating the period-3 window: r = 1+sqrt(8). Computed: Newton solve of f^3(x)=x, (f^3)'(x)=+1 from (x,r)=(0.5144,3.8284).

End of the stable 3-cycle (period doubling 3->6, multiplier of the 3-cycle = -1). Value: Newton continuation with analytic derivatives at 240-bit precision; computed: independent mpmath solve with numerical differentiation.

Smallest point of the attracting 3-cycle at r=3.83 (the other two are 0.504666487408 and 0.957416597519; multiplier 0.329882). Reference: mp Newton on f^3(x)=x. Computed: plain double iteration from x0=0.5, 100000 steps, then minimum of the next 3 iterates.
Parameter where the two chaotic bands merge into one (Misiurewicz point: f^3(1/2) equals the fixed point 1-1/r); real root of r^3-2r^2-4r-8=0. Computed: Newton solve of f^3(1/2) = 1-1/r.
Lower point of the attracting 2-cycle at r=3.2: (r+1-sqrt((r-3)(r+1)))/(2r); upper point is 0.799455490467370. Computed: iterate x0=0.2 for 2000 steps, take min of next two iterates.
Lyapunov exponent on the stable 2-cycle at r=3.2: (1/2) ln|4+2r-r^2| = (1/2) ln 0.16. Computed: mean of ln|r(1-2x_n)| over 100000 steps after 1000 transient from x0=0.2.

Lyapunov exponent at r=4 is ln 2. Method: mean of ln|r(1-2x_n)| over N=1e6 steps after 1000 transient. Observed over 32 initial conditions in (0.05,0.95): sd 1.7e-06, max |dev| 4.5e-06 (the sum telescopes at r=4, so convergence is O(1/N)).
oracles.source: exact: ln 2 (conjugacy with the tent map)

oracles.description: Lyapunov exponent at r=3.9. Method as lyapunov-r4 (N=1e6 after 1000 transient). Value = mean over 32 initial conditions; observed sd 4.4e-04, max |dev| 9.6e-04.
Time average of x at r=4 is 1/2 (invariant density 1/(pi sqrt(x(1-x)))); the variance is 1/8 (measured 0.12498). N=1e6 after 1000 transient; over 32 initial conditions sd 3.5e-04, max |dev| 1.2e-03.
x_8 from x_0=0.2 at r=4, plain iteration x <- r*x*(1-x) (x_1=0.64, x_2=0.9216). Reference value from 50-digit arithmetic; rounding-error amplification bound 640.
x_10 from x_0=0.5 at r=3.9, plain iteration (x_1=0.975). Reference from 50-digit arithmetic; amplification bound 216.
Fixed point in x>0: x = 1/(1+a-b), y = b*x = 0.227272727272727, at a=1.7, b=0.5 (saddle inside the attractor). Computed: numerical root of the map equations.
Fixed point in x<0: x = 1/(1-a-b), y = b*x = -0.416666666666667 (exists when a+b>1).

Largest Lyapunov exponent at a=1.7, b=0.5 (per-step QR with J = [[-a*sign(x), 1],[b, 0]], N=1e6 after 1000 transient). Value: mean of 12 runs of 1e8 steps. Scatter at N=1e6 over 32 initial conditions: sd 3.5e-04, max |dev| 6.5e-04.
Second Lyapunov exponent, same method. Scatter at N=1e6: sd 3.5e-04, max |dev| 6.5e-04.
lam1 + lam2 = ln|det J| = ln(b) = ln 0.5 for any orbit (det J = -b). Computed from a 1e6-step QR run; allowed deviation 1e-9.
x_10 from (0,0) at a=1.7, b=0.5, simultaneous update (x,y) <- (1-a*|x|+y, b*x); first steps (1,0), (-0.7,0.5). Reference from 50-digit arithmetic; amplification bound 246.
y_10 of the same orbit (equals b*x_9).
First period doubling: the fixed point x*=1 has multiplier 1-r, equal to -1 at r=2. Computed: independent mpmath solve of f(x)=x, f'(x)=-1.
Second period doubling (2-cycle multiplier = -1). Value: Newton solve with analytic derivatives at 240-bit precision; computed: independent mpmath solve with numerical differentiation.
Third period doubling (4-cycle multiplier = -1). Value: Newton solve with analytic derivatives at 240-bit precision; computed: independent mpmath solve with numerical differentiation.
Fourth period doubling (8-cycle multiplier = -1). Value: Newton solve with analytic derivatives at 240-bit precision; computed: independent mpmath solve with numerical differentiation.
Accumulation point of the period-doubling cascade (onset of chaos). Value: Aitken-extrapolated superstable parameters (k<=12); computed: independent extrapolation of the bifurcation values r_k.
Tangent bifurcation creating the period-3 window: f^3(x)=x with (f^3)'(x)=+1. Value: Newton continuation at 240-bit precision; computed: independent mpmath solve.
Lyapunov exponent at r=3: mean of ln|(1-r x_n) exp(r(1-x_n))| over N=1e6 steps after 1000 transient. Value = mean over 32 initial conditions in (0.05,2.5); observed sd 4.8e-04, max |dev| 9.2e-04.
Upper bound of the attractor is the image of the critical point x_c=1/r: f(1/r) = exp(r-1)/r; value for r=3 (lower bound f(f(1/r)) = 0.030572). Computed: maximum of a 2e6-step orbit from x0=0.5.
x_8 from x_0=0.5 at r=3, plain iteration x <- x*exp(r*(1-x)). Reference from 50-digit arithmetic; amplification bound 379.
x=0 loses stability (f'(0) = r*pi = 1) at r = 1/pi; for larger r a positive fixed point exists. Computed: root of r*pi*cos(0)-1.

First period doubling (1-cycle multiplier = -1). Value: Newton solve with analytic derivatives at 240-bit precision; computed: independent mpmath solve of f^p(x)=x, (f^p)'(x)=-1 using numerical differentiation.
oracles.source: literature r1 = 0.7199616, r2 = 0.8332663 (e.g. Strogatz ex. 10.2.8 style tables)

oracles.description: Second period doubling (2-cycle multiplier = -1). Value: Newton solve with analytic derivatives at 240-bit precision; computed: independent mpmath solve of f^p(x)=x, (f^p)'(x)=-1 using numerical differentiation.
oracles.source: literature r1 = 0.7199616, r2 = 0.8332663 (e.g. Strogatz ex. 10.2.8 style tables)

oracles.description: Third period doubling (4-cycle multiplier = -1). Value: Newton solve with analytic derivatives at 240-bit precision; computed: independent mpmath solve of f^p(x)=x, (f^p)'(x)=-1 using numerical differentiation.
oracles.source: literature r1 = 0.7199616, r2 = 0.8332663 (e.g. Strogatz ex. 10.2.8 style tables)

oracles.description: Fourth period doubling (8-cycle multiplier = -1). Value: Newton solve with analytic derivatives at 240-bit precision; computed: independent mpmath solve of f^p(x)=x, (f^p)'(x)=-1 using numerical differentiation.
oracles.source: literature r1 = 0.7199616, r2 = 0.8332663 (e.g. Strogatz ex. 10.2.8 style tables)

oracles.description: Accumulation point of the period-doubling cascade. Value: Aitken-extrapolated superstable parameters R_k (k<=13); computed: independent extrapolation of the bifurcation values r_k.

Universality: the ratios (r_(k-1)-r_(k-2))/(r_k-r_(k-1)) of this non-quadratic-polynomial map converge to the same Feigenbaum delta as the logistic map; (r3-r2)/(r4-r3) = 4.628709. Computed: Aitken-extrapolated ratio of superstable parameters up to period 2^13.
Lyapunov exponent at r=1: mean of ln|r*pi*cos(pi x_n)| over N=1e6 steps after 1000 transient. Value = mean over 32 initial conditions in (0.05,0.95); observed sd 8.0e-05, max |dev| 1.9e-04.
x_7 from x_0=0.3 at r=1, plain iteration x <- r*sin(pi*x). Reference from 50-digit arithmetic; amplification bound 148.
x_8 from x_0=0.3 at r=0.9. Reference from 50-digit arithmetic; amplification bound 105.

Time average of x at mu=2 is 1/2 (uniform invariant density; variance 1/12, measured 0.08339). Iterate with mu clamped to 2-1e-12 (exact 2 collapses to 0 in binary floating point), N=1e6 after 1000 transient; over 32 initial conditions sd 3.2e-04, max |dev| 8.2e-04.

Lyapunov exponent equals ln(mu) for every orbit because |f'(x)| = mu on both branches; here mu=1.5 (at mu=2 it is ln 2 = 0.693147...). Computed: orbit average of ln|central difference of f| (h=1e-7) over 100000 steps after 1000 transient from x0=0.3.
Nonzero fixed point x* = mu/(1+mu) (exists for mu>1, always repelling); value for mu=1.5. Computed: bisection root of f(x)-x on [0.55,0.65].

For 1<mu<sqrt(2) the attractor is two bands [c2,c4] and [c3,c1] with c1=mu/2, c2=mu(1-mu/2), c3=mu*c2, c4=mu(1-c3); the gap (c4,c3) closes at mu=sqrt(2). Value: c4 at mu=1.3 (c3=0.591500, c2=0.455000, c1=0.650000). Computed: largest orbit point below x*=mu/(1+mu) over 2e6 steps from x0=0.3.
Band-merging parameter: the two-band attractor becomes a single interval [mu(1-mu/2), mu/2] at mu = sqrt(2). Computed: root of the gap width c3-c4 as a function of mu.
x_8 from x_0=0.1234 at mu=2 (unclamped; 8 steps are far from the 50-step collapse), x <- mu*min(x,1-x). Reference from 50-digit arithmetic; amplification bound 511.
x_10 from x_0=0.3 at mu=1.5. Reference from 50-digit arithmetic; amplification bound 171.

Largest Lyapunov exponent at a=0.9, b=-0.6013, c=2, d=0.5 (per-step QR, J = [[2x+a, -2y+b],[2y+c, 2x+d]], N=1e6 after 1000 transient). Value: mean of 12 runs of 5e7 steps. Scatter at N=1e6 over 32 initial conditions on the attractor: sd 2.4e-04, max |dev| 4.5e-04.
Second Lyapunov exponent, same method. Scatter at N=1e6: sd 9.0e-04, max |dev| 2.3e-03.

lam1 + lam2 equals the orbit average of ln|det J| = ln|(2x+a)(2x+d) - (b-2y)(2y+c)| accumulated over the same steps (the determinant is not constant). Value 0 = difference; computed from a 1e6-step run; allowed deviation 1e-9.

(0,0) is a fixed point; DT(0,0) = [[a,b],[c,d]] has complex eigenvalues of modulus sqrt(ad-bc) > 1 (unstable focus), so an orbit started exactly at the origin never leaves it while nearby points spiral out. Computed: numpy eigenvalues of the Jacobian at the origin.
x_12 from (x_0,y_0)=(-0.72,-0.64) at a=0.9, b=-0.6013, c=2, d=0.5, simultaneous update. Reference from 50-digit arithmetic; amplification bound 179.
y_12 of the same orbit.
